purpose: Who may open a job in Aaron's ledger by messaging him. Replaces the blunt --max-jobs cap with a sender tiering; the cap remains as a backstop.

known: address or number, or sha256:<hex of lowercase address> — people whose messages may open jobs
blocked: archived unread, never folded into the thread

actions.job: fold into the thread and open a reply job when a reply is owed (subject to max_jobs_per_run)
actions.note: fold into the thread as data only; never opens a job
actions.archive: move to processed/blocked without folding; nothing enters the ledger

signing.rule: When the secret is set (or --require-signed), only drops whose _verified.mac validates are folded; unsigned or edited files go to processed/unverified.

notes: The senders file is personal (it lists who writes to Aaron) and lives in the git-ignored identity/aaron/local/. Hashes are accepted so it need not hold plaintext addresses.
Until Aaron curates a known list, unknown senders keep opening (capped) jobs so the bridge stays useful; once a known list exists, strangers become thread notes automatically.
Guest principals get their own senders file under data/principals/<id>/inkbox/senders.json.
